question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is reviewing a 3-stock price-weighted index used by Satpura Market-Neutral Fund as a regional sub-benchmark. On Day 0: Stock P INR 120, Stock Q INR 180, Stock R INR 300 (divisor 6). On Day 1: P INR 132, Q INR 198, R INR 330 (no corporate actions, divisor unchanged). What is the Day-1 value of this price-weighted index?

explanation.text: The Logic: Day-0 sum = 120+180+300 = 600; index_0 = 600/6 = 100. Day-1 sum = 132+198+330 = 660; index_1 = 660/6 = 110. Each constituent rose 10%, so the price-weighted index also rose 10% — from 100 to 110. The Trap: Option A is the Day-0 base value. Option B (105) is the average of a mis-computed 5% rise. Option D (115.50) would be if someone incorrectly applied 10% twice (compounded) on the base. The price-weighted formula is simply sum of prices / adjusted divisor. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (PM) tests price-weighted index mechanics for benchmarking PMS portfolios. XIX-C / XIX-D cover it for All-Cat / Cat I/II contexts. Same formula everywhere.
